IBM.rationale: IBM presents a genuine but incomplete fundamental inflection. Q1 2026 YoY revenue growth of +9.5%, EPS growth of +14.3%, and OCF growth of +18.3% confirm real business momentum. A dramatic profitability step-up is visible in the ratio data: net margin jumped from ~9% to 15.6% and ROE from ~21% to 32.5% between April and May 2026, likely reflecting a trailing earnings restatement capturing a higher-earnings period. P/E at 24.3x sits at the low end of its 19-51x one-year range, having compressed ~50% on earnings growth rather than price decline. However, IBM's earnings yield (4.1%) sits below the 10-year Treasury yield (4.45%), offering no valuation cushion in a high-rate environment. Leverage remains elevated (D/E 3.73x total liabilities, ~1.75x debt-only). The February 2026 AI-driven single-day crash exposed fragility in market confidence around mainframe franchise durability. Revenue growth of 9.5% lags the peer average of 12.43%. The gap between watsonx AI bookings ($12B+ inception-to-date) and recognized recurring AI revenue remains opaque. Franchise quality is real — Red Hat OpenShift as #1 enterprise Kubernetes, IBM Z irreplaceability in mission-critical financial infrastructure, 95% Fortune 500 penetration — but constrained by hyperscaler competition and AI disruption risk. Near-term catalysts include the ServiceNow and Google Cloud AI partnerships (June 2026) and the $10B quantum investment commitment, but these are long-dated and do not constitute near-term re-rating events. The stock is mildly attractive: solid fundamentals with improving trajectory, fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation vs own history, but no compelling value entry given the earnings yield below risk-free rate and unresolved leverage concerns.
